01.r: Two human beings, introduced without names.
01.n: The general word for a human being. The Greek puts it first: 'men, two, went up'.

02.r: A pair, to be set side by side.

03.n: Abbott-Smith gives 'to go up, ascend', and cites this verse for going up into the temple with an infinitive of purpose. That the 'up' reflects the temple's height is a reasonable reading.

06.r: The temple and its courts, where people came to pray.
06.n: The neuter of the adjective 'sacred', used as a noun. Abbott-Smith gives the adjective's sense 'consecrated to the deity, sacred'. This study keeps 'temple' for this word and 'sanctuary' for ναός.

07.n: Abbott-Smith notes that the verb is always used of prayer to God (or, in classical writers, to gods).

08.r: With 'one', picks out the first of the pair.

10.r: A member of the party known for strict keeping of the law.

11.r: Sets the second man beside the first.

12.r: With 'other', picks out the second of the pair.

13.n: Abbott-Smith explains the word as properly denoting the second of a pair, with the article 'the other', as here.

14.r: A man of the toll trade, set against the Pharisee.
14.n: Abbott-Smith cites this verse under his second sense: a subordinate who collected taxes or tolls in a particular district. This study renders it 'toll collector' throughout.
